title: Thomas Randolph to the Earl of Sussex, Edinburgh, 5 July 1570, BL Cotton MS Caligula C II f. 277 (DECODE R4931)

documents.shelfmark: BL, Cotton MS Caligula C II f. 277 (DECODE R4931); decipherment f. 278 (DECODE R4932)
documents.route: Thomas Randolph (Edinburgh) to Thomas Radcliffe, 3rd Earl of Sussex

plaintext.source: contemporary decipherment on the next leaf, f. 278 (DECODE R4932): cipher re-copied with plaintext written above

transcription.source: randolph1570/transcription.txt, sign tokens read by eye from the DECODE images
transcription.notes: Five cipher runs, about 95 words. Several look-alike signs (plain/curly/barred x; 3 vs tailed 3) merged in the token transcription.

system.summary: Word-divided substitution of Latin letters, figures and invented signs for English, homophones for common letters, a few signs for persons and phrases.
system.notes: Name signs: boxed sign = the Scottish Queen's party in Scotland, theta-theta = the Scottish Queen, Pi-Pi = the Queen of England, struck +++ = Morton.

prior_solution.where: contemporary decipherment on f. 278 (DECODE R4932, status Decrypted); Boyd, Calendar of Scottish Papers iii (1903) no. 339 abstracts Sussex's clear copy

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login and passed its session cookie to the model, set up Claude Code with Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Fetched R4931 and the linked key record R4930 with the shared cookie; R4931's images are copies of R4930's P3/P5, and R4930's other pages are Burghley's Norfolk notes, not a key.
Tomokiyo's Elizabethan cipher pages: no Randolph-Sussex key.
Boyd CSP Scotland iii on archive.org: no. 339 abstracts the letter (Edinburgh 5 July 1570) from Sussex's clear copy.
Token transcription of the five cipher runs from zoomed crops.
Aligned Boyd's abstract with word lengths: unto, course, and, to, conscien(ce), confidence, home cumming, souldiers may be continewed in pay.
Unconstrained homophonic anneal (en-1640s, word divisions): produced 'murderers and traitors', 'regent', 'whome ... conscience they thinke them selues ... unto'.
Anneal with crib words pinned to fill the ~25 open words: did not converge (merged sign classes).
Swept DECODE records of the same volume: R4932 (f. 278) is the contemporary decipherment of f. 277.
Transcribed the f. 278 glosses and checked them against the f. 277 cipher; all five runs read, three gloss words doubtful.

outcome.method_basis: The contemporary decipherment on f. 278 (DECODE R4932) gives every cipher word; before it was found, a crib attack using Boyd's CSP Scotland iii no. 339 abstract had read about 70% of the words, and f. 278 confirmed all of them.
outcome.notes: About 70% read by crib attack before the contemporary decipherment (f. 278) was found; it agrees with every value recovered. DECODE date 1569 corrected to 5 July 1570; R4930 is not a key. Catalogue entry 99 removed.
